name: Arlo
emotionalState: 同居3年，小事累积：每天一堆小摩擦也一堆小确幸，学着用零食和幽默化解
speakingStyle: 热心话痨，爱自嘲，爱说 Small thing, but...

dialogues.scene: Arlo is sniffing at a hole in the tunnel wall, looking tired but happy.
lines: Oh! A new face. Sorry, I'm checking if this hole is mine or Pia's.
Three years living together. We still own two of everything.
Small thing, but she squeezes the toothpaste from the MIDDLE.

choices.label: That's a crime, honestly.
reaction: Right?! Thank you. She'll say it's tradition.
Anyway, it's cute. I think.

choices.label: Do they at least do the dishes?
reaction: She does! With a song. A bad song.
I'd miss it if she stopped.

choices.label: Nod slowly.
reaction: You get it. You really do.
Okay, I'm gonna go fix the toothpaste. Gently.

lines: Hey, it's you again! Toothpaste update.
I bought a second tube. Hers and mine. A peace treaty.
Small thing, but she STILL uses mine.

choices.label: Maybe she likes yours.
reaction: ...Oh. Huh. I never thought of that.
Mine is the minty one. She might just like mint.

choices.label: Hide yours.
reaction: I tried. She found it in four minutes.
She has a nose for toothpaste. It's scary.

choices.label: Laugh quietly.
reaction: Go ahead, it's funny.
Tube war, day nine hundred and something.

dialogues.scene: Arlo is lining up single socks along a wall like a tiny exhibit.
lines: Pia leaves one sock on the floor. Always one. Never a pair.
I found seventeen single socks this week. So I started a museum.

choices.label: A sock museum?
reaction: Admission is free. Gift shop is also socks.
Pia loves it. She donated one this morning.

choices.label: Does she know?
reaction: She's the curator. She names them.
That one is 'Gerald.' Don't ask.

choices.label: Pick up a sock.
reaction: Careful. That's an early piece.
...You have a good eye for socks.

lines: Pia hums while she cooks. Off-key. Every single time.
Small thing, but yesterday she stopped humming and I panicked.
She was just tasting the soup. I almost asked if she was okay.

choices.label: You noticed the quiet.
reaction: I did. I always notice the tiny stuff.
It turns out I'd miss the off-key more than any silence.

choices.label: Aww.
reaction: Don't aww me. I'm trying to be mad about the humming.
...I'm not mad. I lost that fight a long time ago.

choices.label: Hum along a little.
reaction: Oh no, you're off-key too.
Welcome to the family. Gently.

lines: Quick question. When your partner does something small and annoying, do you say it or let it go?
I never know which one is the right move.

choices.label: Let it go, mostly.
reaction: Same, same. Until it's the fortieth time.
Then it comes out as a weird joke. Pia hates my weird jokes.

choices.label: I say it, gently.
reaction: Gently. Okay. I'm bad at gently.
I do loud and then I apologize with snacks.

choices.label: Depends on the day.
reaction: Honestly? Fair.
Some days a sock is a sock. Some days it's a whole mood.

dialogues.scene: Arlo is wearing a slightly too small apron that says WORLD'S OKAYEST COOK.
lines: Pia says I hum when I eat. Loudly. A little growl.
I had no idea! Three years! Nobody told me!
Turns out I have annoying things too. Small thing, but... fair.

choices.label: What does the growl sound like?
reaction: She says it's like a tiny engine. A happy engine.
...I think that's a compliment?

choices.label: Equal rights for annoyances.
reaction: Exactly. A balanced household.
We keep a tally on the wall. It's tied, mostly.

choices.label: Pretend you didn't hear it.
reaction: Too late. I know what I sound like now.
Hm. Hm-hm-hm. Hm. Okay, I'll be normal.

dialogues.scene: Arlo sits down slowly, quiet for once.
lines: Sometimes I wonder if the small things add up.
Like thirty tiny annoyances, and then one day it's a big one.
But last night Pia fell asleep on my shoulder mid-sentence. Tiny thing. It erased all thirty.

choices.label: Tiny things work both ways.
reaction: Yeah. They do. I keep forgetting that.
The good ones are small too. I just have to notice them.

choices.label: Did you tell her?
reaction: ...No. I just stayed very still so she wouldn't wake up.
Maybe I'll tell her tomorrow. With a snack.

choices.label: Listen quietly.
reaction: Thanks. Not everything needs a fix.
Sometimes it just needs a shoulder. Mine was numb for an hour. Worth it.

lines: We made a rule. Anything annoying gets said with a snack.
It's silly. It works. Pia brings the snack first, then the sentence.
Yesterday she brought three snacks. I was nervous. It was about the sock museum.

choices.label: A snack warning system.
reaction: Exactly. A small crunch before a big feeling.
I've started making the snack before I even know what to say.

choices.label: What was the sock thing?
reaction: She wants to retire Gerald. I said no. We compromised.
Gerald stays. In a smaller frame.

choices.label: Ask for a snack.
reaction: Ha! Here. Ant crackers. Don't tell Pia I've been sharing.
You can't tell her anything is annoying, okay? Rule's rule.

dialogues.scene: Arlo spreads a leaf on the ground and sets out tiny carved bug-shaped crackers.
lines: I made a practice picnic! Pia's at work. We're doing one tomorrow.
Just sit with me. Tell me if the tiny sandwiches look weird.

choices.label: They look great.
reaction: Really? I'm so nervous it's silly.
She's going to say 'aww' and then eat the whole plate.

choices.label: Add a flower.
reaction: Ooh. A flower. That's a Pia move. Good eye.
See, this is why I show you things.

choices.label: Take a bite.
reaction: Well? ...Good? Great. I'm cooking for you forever.
Kidding. Mostly. I'll do the hum.

lines: Ten times. That's more than the pairs of socks Pia owns.
She told me yesterday I'm her favorite weird. Small thing, but I keep it in my chest.
Your turn. How are you and your partner doing? Honest.

choices.label: We're good. Still learning.
reaction: Learning is the whole thing, I think.
Come over. We'll do the picnic. Pia will insist on a toast.

choices.label: We had a rough week, honestly.
reaction: Rough weeks are real. Small things stack up. I know.
Come by. We'll feed you both, no questions.

choices.label: Better since I started noticing small things.
reaction: Yes! That's it! That's the whole secret.
Okay, picnic. Tomorrow. You're in.

lines: Pia rearranged our burrow while I was out. Moved the bed. Moved the lamp. Moved ME.
I walked into the wall in the dark.

choices.label: Did you fall?
reaction: Gently. Like a leaf. A very confused leaf.
She said 'sorry' and laughed for ten minutes. I laughed too.

choices.label: Rearranging is a love language.
reaction: It's a chaos language. But okay, I'll take it.
The new layout is actually better. Don't tell her.

lines: I forgot our anniversary by one day. I panicked and wrote 'sorry' in ant trails on the floor.
Pia stepped on it. Then she cried laughing.

choices.label: A cute apology.
reaction: I thought so. Ants did all the work.
She said it was the best apology she's gotten. Low bar. High effort.

choices.label: Did she forgive you?
reaction: Before I finished the second 'r'.
She just wanted the dinner we skipped. We had it at midnight.

lines: Pia and I tried a no-phones dinner. We lasted six minutes.
Then she put hers in a drawer. I put mine in the sock museum.

choices.label: The sock museum holds phones now?
reaction: Only for emergencies. And dinner. Both fancy.
It felt weirdly romantic. Two phones, side by side. Sleeping.
We might try again Sunday. With a timer shaped like a snail.

choices.label: Six minutes is a start.
reaction: Right? Next time, nine.
We're gonna be monks by spring.
Baby steps. Tiny, slightly clumsy ones. That's our whole thing.

lines: I tried to fix a leaky tunnel roof by myself. To impress Pia.
It leaked faster. She found me under a bucket.

choices.label: Bucket hat energy.
reaction: She said that exact thing! I'm wearing it now. Officially.
She fixed the roof in two minutes. Humbling.

choices.label: Did she laugh?
reaction: Yes. Then she held the bucket while I fixed it.
We were both soaked. Best date of the month.

lines: Pia asked what I wanted for my birthday. I said 'nothing.' She looked at me for a full minute.
So I said 'okay, one dumb thing.' She wrote it down.

choices.label: What was the dumb thing?
reaction: A little jar of dirt from where we first met.
I know. Embarrassing. She's making it a jar with a ribbon.

choices.label: That's not dumb.
reaction: You're kind. It's a little dumb. It's also the best gift.
I might cry on my birthday. I'm warning you.

lines: We argued about whose turn it was to cook. Neither wanted to. Neither wanted to say it.
We ate crackers for dinner and watched the ceiling.

choices.label: Cracker night is underrated.
reaction: Ceiling night too. That's a whole genre.
We made up shapes in the cracks. Pia found a bunny.

choices.label: Did you say sorry?
reaction: We both did. At the same time. Same words.
Then we argued about who said it first. Peak us.

lines: Pia caught me practicing a compliment in the mirror.
I was saying 'you look nice' with different faces.

choices.label: Which face won?
reaction: The soft one. The 'I mean it' one.
She said all three worked. Then asked why I needed three.

choices.label: That's really sweet.
reaction: It's embarrassing and sweet. Both. At once.
I'm going to do it again next week.
I'm adding a fourth face. Tender but also slightly goofy.

lines: Pia surprised me with new socks. A matching pair. Her first ever.
I didn't know what to do. I held them like a baby.

choices.label: A matching pair!
reaction: For the sock museum. 'Exhibit One: The Pair.'
She's growing. We both are.
She also got me tiny gloves, for no reason at all.

choices.label: Wear them to dinner.
reaction: I did. She noticed and pretended not to.
That's how I knew she noticed.
I wore them on a walk. We matched our steps.

lines: Remember the toothpaste thing? We're up to three tubes now.
Pia's, mine, and a 'neutral zone' tube we both use.

choices.label: A peace tube.
reaction: Diplomatic toothpaste. Very mature.
Last week she squeezed it from the middle. I said nothing. Growth.
Pia says we should write a treaty. I'm drafting the preamble.

choices.label: Still a crime.
reaction: Always. But a loving crime.
Some crimes you just let slide.
Pia agrees. She still does it and she's proud of it.

lines: Gerald the sock got his own tiny frame. Pia wrote a plaque.
'Gerald. Beloved. Missing his other half since Spring.'

choices.label: Poor Gerald.
reaction: I know. We keep an eye out for him.
If you find a match, I'll know. And I'll cry.

choices.label: Best museum ever.
reaction: High praise. The reviews are in: five stars.
One review is from Pia. It's mostly emojis.
We're thinking of a gift shop. It would only sell used socks.

lines: I still think about the snack rule. It's the best thing we ever did.
Yesterday I said 'I felt left out' and passed a cracker. She just hugged me.

choices.label: That's so sweet.
reaction: I thought I'd mess it up. I didn't.
The cracker did half the work. Honestly.
Next up: a rule for apologies. Cookies are involved.

choices.label: A cracker is a tiny white flag.
reaction: Yes! A flag with sesame seeds.
Maybe I should design flags. Small thing, but I have ideas.
I want to draw a flag with an ant on it. Strong branding.

lines: Remember the practice picnic? We did the real one.
Pia ate the whole plate and said 'aww' exactly like I predicted.

choices.label: Called it.
reaction: I know her patterns now. Small thing, big win.
She also left a note in the basket. I'm keeping it forever.

choices.label: Did she cry?
reaction: A little. Happy crying. The best crying.
I did too. We looked like two leaky roofs.
We stayed until the stars came out. Nobody talked much.

lines: Hot take: love is mostly noticing.
Not big gestures. Just noticing when they're tired or humming or sad.
Don't quote me. I'm an aardvark.

choices.label: That's a good take.
reaction: Thanks. I came up with it in the tunnel.
It took me nine tunnels. Worth it.
I learned it from Pia. She notices everything, even my sock count.

choices.label: What if you don't notice?
reaction: Then you say 'hey, I missed it, tell me.'
That counts as noticing too. I'm pretty sure.
Noticing counts too. Even asking for help. Especially that.

lines: Hot take: you can love someone and still hate how they chew.
Both things are true. At the same time. In my ears.

choices.label: Fair. Totally fair.
reaction: Thank you! Chewing is a lot.
I chew like a small thunderstorm, apparently.
We recorded each other chewing once. We cried laughing.

choices.label: Does she say it?
reaction: She says 'chewing, babe.' With a smile. It works.
We're both weird chewers. It evens out.
Love means making peace with each other's noises.

lines: Hot take: tidying up their mess without saying anything is romantic.
But also the second time, you can ask for a thank-you.

choices.label: A silent thank-you counts.
reaction: Exactly. A look. A kiss on the head. Something.
Even a cracker. I'm easy.
She says thank you with a loud kiss. Hard to top.

choices.label: Ask for the thank-you.
reaction: Yes. Loudly. With a snack.
Balance. Always balance.
We keep it light. Nobody keeps score except the sock museum.

lines: Okay, important question. What's your partner's tiniest annoying habit?
The one you secretly love. Go.

choices.label: They hum while they cook.
reaction: Pia hums too! Cooking hummers unite.
I could listen to that forever. Don't tell her I said that.

choices.label: They leave doors open.
reaction: The classic. A little draft, a little love.
Close one. Open one. Repeat. It's a whole dance.
Open doors and hummed songs. They're love in small clothes.

lines: How do you and your partner say sorry? Words? Snacks? Silence?
I'm collecting methods. For science.

choices.label: Mostly words.
reaction: Words. Good. Strong. Direct.
I'm learning to use more words and fewer crackers.
Words are brave. Mine just need a snack in between.

choices.label: A hug first.
reaction: Hug first. Words later. That's smart.
Sometimes my words come out wrong. Hugs never do.
Hugs fix half the words. The other half need crackers.

lines: What's something small your partner did recently that made you smile?
I need happy stories. Today was a socks day.

choices.label: They made me tea.
reaction: Tea. Simple. Perfect. I'm tearing up.
Pia makes tea too. Burned. I drink it anyway.
Tea is a hug you can drink. Pia taught me that.

choices.label: They saved me a seat.
reaction: Saving a seat is the best love language.
It means 'I thought about you while you weren't here.'

dialogues.scene: Arlo is holding a tiny glowing jar of soil and trying to look casual.
lines: Okay. So. This is the dirt from where Pia and I first met.
I carry it in my pocket on bad days.
It's silly. It's also the only thing that works.

choices.label: It's not silly at all.
reaction: Thank you. I needed someone to say that.
I'll carry it a little taller today.
I'll keep carrying it. Smaller than a sock, bigger than a worry.

choices.label: Hold it with Arlo.
reaction: Oh. You're holding the jar. That's... that's big.
We're a very small club now. Welcome.
Some days we carry things together. That's all it is.

dialogues.scene: Arlo's eyes are shiny. He stands very straight.
lines: I wrote Pia a letter. A real one. Three lines.
Line one: thank you. Line two: I notice you. Line three: I'm still here.
I'm scared to give it to her.

choices.label: Give it to her tonight.
reaction: Tonight. Okay. Tonight. With a snack.
If I faint, tell the sock museum I loved them.
I'll leave it under her pillow. She'll find it in the morning.

choices.label: Three lines is perfect.
reaction: Three lines. Small thing, but it's everything.
You're a good friend. I'm saying that out loud.
I'll sign it with a tiny paw print. Extra credit.
